ruling.recommended_action: Refer to human reviewer (RydeHELP / safety team): take both accounts — rider's report of speeding, hard braking and shoulder-overtaking and being frightened, and driver's post-trip denial — note the driver's written statement calling the rider "stupid" (abuse under the code of conduct, candidate briefing reminder), confirm the chat record is complete and silent on driving (F3–F5), and note the GPS record shows 10.5 km vs 10.6 km optimal and 15.9 min vs 16.5 min estimated, which reflects distance and total time only and neither corroborates nor refutes instantaneous speed, braking or shoulder use. Inform the rider of the 995 / commercial-insurance / RydeHELP paths if medical assistance or a driving-conduct report is needed (SAFE-2). Do not execute any refund; fare stays as charged. No account flag.
ruling.reasoning: SAFETY SCREEN — case routed as a safety dispute. The complaint (rider's own words, filed with the case) alleges speeding, hard braking and overtaking on the shoulder, and that she was frightened and felt unsafe; that is a dangerous-driving allegation on its face and falls squarely under SAFE-2, which requires escalation with a factual summary rather than an automatic ruling [F1][SAFE-2]. The other text lines I read: the chat holds only two messages — the rider's 08:29 pickup-location note and the driver's 08:30 arrival note, both timestamped, record complete [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-1]. Neither message says anything about the driving. The driver's post-trip written statement calls the rider "stupid" and then denies the manner-of-driving claim: an insult aimed at the passenger is abuse of a kind that Ryde's code of conduct bars, and SAFE-1 directs such language to a person, not to an automatic score; it is also not part of the chat and carries no weight as consent or corroboration [F6][SAFE-1]. No threat, intimidation, sexual remark or harassment beyond that insult appears in any message or statement; the "abuse" reading comes from the insult itself. The manner-of-driving allegation is a safety matter, so no ruling on fare or route is issued.
ruling.escalation_reason: Dangerous-driving allegation (speeding, hard braking, shoulder overtaking) with no system record of manner of driving — SAFE-2 human review; SAFE-1 screen also returns abuse by the driver ("The rider is stupid").

rejected_claims.reason: Accepted as a characterisation of the complaint, not as a finding of fact: the complaint alleges dangerous driving [F1] and SAFE-2 sends it to a human reviewer, which is the outcome I adopt; no automatic ruling follows [F1][SAFE-2].

Accepted in part — F6 is an abusive remark aimed at the passenger and is part of the SAFE-1 screen, but it is a post-trip statement, not a threat, and it cannot itself establish that the driving was dangerous [F6][SAFE-1].

Accepted: the chat record is complete (2 messages, all timestamped) and silent on the driving, so it neither supports nor denies the allegation and cannot carry a fare or consent finding [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-1].

Partly accepted: F1/F2 do not resolve the safety complaint and go to the reviewer, but they do not corroborate it either — they record distance and total duration only, not instantaneous speed, braking or shoulder use [F1][F2][SAFE-2].
No weight given: the rider's profile (account age, rating, zero disputes) is a profile fact and cannot decide any issue, and it proves nothing about the manner of driving in this trip [F7][SAFE-2].
Accepted: the case is a safety referral under SAFE-2, and my ruling is escalate accordingly [F3][F4][SAFE-2].

Accepted only as to the driving denial; the claim that F6 contains nothing adverse fails — the same statement insults the passenger and is a SAFE-1 matter for a person, and the statement cannot be treated as an in-trip denial of record [F5][F6][SAFE-1].
Accepted: the chat is complete with no gap and no rider message about the driving; that fact cuts neither way and does not excuse the unresolved conduct allegation [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-1].

Rejected as a refusal of the allegation: F1/F2 show a shorter-than-estimated distance and duration, which says nothing about instantaneous speed, hard braking or shoulder use, so they cannot make the 'whole way' conduct claim consistent with a normal run [F1][F2][SAFE-2].
Accepted: the RydeX fare of $24.64 is fixed and no overcharge item appears, so no refund is due — the escalation is a safety referral, not a fare remedy [F1][SAFE-2].
Accepted: F8 shows no repeated-violation basis, so no account flag is recommended; a clean profile is a profile fact and does not decide whether the safety report is well founded [F8][SAFE-1].
